exactIssue: A Codex executor derived 76 non-validation questionnaire records by arithmetic and silently upgraded that artifact observation into the scientific acceptance rule that a complete profile requires 76 items. No owner or reasoning-chat directive selected that denominator, and production scoring actually exposes 27 frozen rules spanning 23 unique question IDs. The unauthorized criterion then entered owner-facing prose and independent-review premises as if it were established authority.

relevantRule.section: Machine-checkable dual alignment and typed completion
relevantRule.excerpt: Every material requirement must be mapped, explicitly amended/removed by the owner, or escalated.

observedOrHypotheticalFailure: Authentic owner-source receipts and dual alignment did not prevent an executor-added numeric specificity from becoming a scientific criterion. Worker-to-contract can remain GREEN after the inference is copied into the contract, synthetic tests can validate the mechanics without validating production cardinality, and later reviewers can inherit the producer-supplied number rather than reproduce it. This can falsely authorize scientific readiness or release while the actual acceptance rule remains unresolved.

evidenceRefs.finding: 81 total and 76 non-validation are question-bank facts; 23 unique mapped IDs is a production scoring fact; neither number is an authorized scientific completeness criterion.

evidenceRefs.observation: The browser runtime returned no available browser instances, so no signed-in Pro meta-review verdict was obtained.

proposedChange: Add claim-level provenance with explicit authority and claim-kind typing; treat every executor-added denominator, threshold, sample size, validation phase, or evidence-sufficiency rule as unauthorized unless enumerated in a current owner or reasoning-chat directive; add reconciliation states UNAUTHORIZED_ADDITION, INFERRED_NUMERIC_SCOPE, and DERIVATION_UNVERIFIED; rerun objective reconciliation whenever a load-bearing numeric or scientific criterion changes; require production-artifact cardinality evidence and independent reproduction; prevent synthetic fixtures from satisfying production-cardinality evidence; and reject definitive owner-facing rendering of unregistered claims.

alternativesConsidered.alternative: Treat all non-validation questionnaire records as required
alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That selects a scientific burden and completeness rule without authority and conflates acquisition scope with production scoring scope.

alternativesConsidered.alternative: Use the 23 mapped production IDs as the completeness rule
alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That is an artifact-derived fact, not an owner- or reasoning-authorized scientific criterion.

alternativesConsidered.alternative: Rely on independent review to catch incorrect counts
alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: The reviewer can inherit the producer number unless every load-bearing cardinality must be independently reproduced before it enters the review premise.

risks: Claim registries can become ceremonial unless definitive rendering and directive admission fail closed.
Not every qualitative refinement can be classified mechanically; semantic equivalence still belongs to Extra High or Pro.
Overbroad numeric gating could burden harmless implementation constants, so the control is limited to load-bearing acceptance, scientific, product, and release claims.
The proposed change has not yet received the required shared Pro meta-review verdict.
workerRecommendation: Extra High recommends immediate adoption of the claim-authority guardrails and hostile tests on a draft Mission Control branch, with canonical integration held until the shared Pro meta-review returns a validated verdict.
workerUncertainty: The exact runtime storage location for the claim registry may vary by Mission Control implementation. The authority distinction and failure mode are not uncertain; neither 23 nor 76 is currently an authorized scientific completeness criterion.
decisionThatCanChange: Whether Mission Control admits executor-derived numeric specificity into task contracts, owner-facing scientific statements, reviewer premises, or release criteria without explicit reasoning authority and independently reproduced production evidence.
